correctness.rationale: For finite nonempty reflexive antisymmetric height<=2 Kripke partial orders and k>=1, q=2^k, a pointed state of colour r either collapses bisimilarly to terminal t_r when strict-successor colours lie in {r}, or is identified uniquely by (r,S), S containing at least one off-colour successor, giving T=q(2^q-1) bisimulation/modal types. Off-colour successor membership is depth-one definable by Diamond alpha_s. At a nonterminal r-root, eta_r=Diamond(alpha_r AND Box alpha_r), a depth-two formula, distinguishes presence/absence of a strict same-colour terminal successor; the root fails Box alpha_r due to the off-colour leaf. Finite disjunctions of type-characteristics realize all 2^T formula classes. Depth-one sees only root colour and reflexive successor colour set, giving q*2^(q-1) distinguishable types, versus q at depth zero. Two models with same {r,s} visible successor colours and different r-terminal existence witness depth-two sharpness. Canonical graph of q terminal states plus all (r,S) representatives has exactly T states and is minimal for a single fixed-coloured model realizing each type. Independently bisimulation-refined the canonical frames for k=1,2,3 yielding (2,4,6), (4,32,60), (8,1024,2040) stages, corroborating but not replacing general proof.
